correctness.rationale: The two symmetric bidegree-(3,3) polynomials are genuinely uniform integral models. Integer elimination shows nested resultants R_A=982087492035469593396623616 and R_B=5838078345771419602547015726577988403024765030400 with gcd 338688=2^8*3^3*7^2, so at least one affine smooth divisor for p outside {2,3,7}. In those three primes the claimed selected Jacobian ideals (f,f_u,f_v) have Groebner basis [1], using B for p=2,3 and A for p=7. The u/v infinity charts have nonzero derivative in v when p!=3, and in t for B when p=3; the corner is absent. Smooth (3,3) ample divisors have genus four, canonical O(1,1), a unique smooth containing quadric. Frobenius factor-swap descends the symmetric divisor to the nonsplit quadric and fixes (0,0); it permutes the two geometric trigonal pencils, while Riemann–Roch on the rational point gives a degree <=4 pencil. Hence every prime-power field admits the asserted genus-four gonality-four example. Source certificates and elimination identities were independently inspected, with actual exact resultant values checked.
residual_risks: Finite prime checks alone are not geometric smoothness proof for all p: the common resultant gcd and boundary chart arguments are required.
The proof gives existence and a construction, not enumeration or uniqueness of genus-four curves.
